common_name: Como Park Rose (Medium Red Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Como Park is a compact, upright Easy Elegance selection that has performed reliably through Minnesota winter trials.

directions: Como Park produces medium-red, double blooms held above dark green, reddish-tinted foliage on a compact, rounded, own-root shrub. It was selected for reliable cold tolerance and is recommended for group plantings where its steady color can anchor a bed or border. Give it full sun and well-drained soil, and prune lightly in late winter to maintain a tidy, upright habit. Being grown on its own roots means winter dieback regrows true to the cultivar rather than from a grafted understock.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Coral Cove Rose (Pink-to-Orange-to-Yellow Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Coral Cove forms a compact, mounded habit well suited to informal hedging.

directions: Coral Cove is an everblooming Easy Elegance selection whose double flowers shift from dark pink outer petals through orange to a bright yellow center, giving each cluster a layered, sunset-like gradient. The small, rounded, own-root shrub stays compact enough for a walkway hedge yet offers enough continuous color for mixed perennial borders. It earned recognition as a Portland Rose Society Best Shrub Rose in 2014 for its strong disease resistance. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil and prune back by about a third in late winter.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Funny Face Rose (Pink and White Painted Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Funny Face produces uniquely patterned pink-and-white blooms where no two flowers match exactly.

directions: Funny Face is named for its playfully irregular two-toned flowers, each petal splashed with pink and white in a pattern that never repeats identically from bloom to bloom. The upright, rounded, own-root shrub keeps clean, disease-resistant foliage through the season and flowers abundantly from late spring into fall. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, and deadhead spent clusters to keep new flushes coming. Light pruning in late winter keeps the rounded habit compact.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Grandma's Blessing Rose (Dusty Pink Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Grandma's Blessing has a symmetrical, vase-shaped habit reminiscent of a hybrid tea, named for Bailey Nurseries founder Margaret 'Grandma' Bailey.

directions: Grandma's Blessing carries large, full, dusty-pink double blooms on dark, glossy, disease-resistant foliage, giving a vase-shaped, own-root shrub the elegant look of a hybrid tea without the fuss of grafted roses. It pairs well with perennials in a mixed border or stands alone as a refined low hedge. The crown stays hardy into zone 4 with winter protection, though zones 5-9 need none. Grow in full sun and well-drained soil, and prune lightly in late winter to maintain its upright form.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Head Over Heels Rose (Light Pink Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Head Over Heels is an upright Easy Elegance selection with full, fluffy light pink flowers that repeat through the season.

directions: Head Over Heels produces full, ruffled light pink blooms, sometimes tinged lavender in cool weather, above dark glossy foliage on an upright, own-root shrub. Its tidy habit and mid-border height make it a natural filler between lower groundcover roses and taller shrubs. Give it full sun, well-drained soil, and a light late-winter pruning to keep the upright form dense. It reblooms steadily from early summer into fall with minimal spray intervention.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: High Voltage Rose (Double Yellow Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; High Voltage grows in a tall, vase-shaped habit well suited to back-of-border placement.

directions: High Voltage bears clustered, double, fragrant yellow blossoms on strong stems above notably clean foliage, standing out among landscape roses for its taller, upright-to-vase-shaped growth. Its height makes it useful as a standalone accent or back-border specimen rather than a low edging plant. The cultivar earned a Portland Rose Society Best Shrub Rose award in 2010 for its vigor and clean growth. Grow in full sun with good drainage, and prune in late winter to control height and encourage fresh flowering wood.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Little Mischief Rose (Deep Pink with White Eye Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Little Mischief is a compact, low-growing Easy Elegance selection whose blooms open deep pink with a white eye and fade lighter as they age.

directions: Little Mischief opens deep pink with a contrasting white eye, and because older and newer blooms appear together, the clusters show a two-tone pink effect through the whole bloom season. The compact, rounded, own-root shrub stays low enough for edging a border, filling a hedge run, or filling a large container. Its lightly fragrant, double flowers appear continuously from late spring through fall with little disease pressure. Plant in full sun and well-drained soil, and shear lightly in late winter to keep the mounded shape tidy.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Mystic Fairy Rose (Red with Pink Undertone Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Mystic Fairy forms a vigorous, rounded mound covered in small, many-petaled red blooms with pink undertones.

directions: Mystic Fairy covers itself in dense clusters of small, richly petaled red flowers carrying pink undertones, set off by new foliage that opens glossy red before maturing to dark green. The vigorous, rounded, own-root shrub reaches a substantial, evenly proportioned mound and resists both blackspot and powdery mildew without regular spraying. Because its flowers are sterile, the plant channels energy into continuous reblooming rather than seed production. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil and prune back by about a third in late winter to maintain density.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Oscar Peterson Rose (Cream-to-White with Golden Center Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Oscar Peterson is a Canadian-bred Easy Elegance selection named for the jazz pianist, with semi-double flowers that open soft cream and whiten as they age.

directions: Oscar Peterson opens semi-double, soft cream-yellow flowers that quickly whiten, each centered with golden stamens, on an upright own-root shrub slightly taller than it is wide. Spent petals drop cleanly from the plant, so it needs little deadheading to stay tidy through a long bloom season from early summer into fall. Its dark green foliage shows strong resistance to common rose diseases. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil; its zone 3 hardiness makes it one of the more cold-tolerant selections in the series.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Paint the Town Rose (Red Hybrid-Tea-Shaped Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Paint the Town has a mounded, spreading habit covered in red hybrid-tea-shaped blooms.

directions: Paint the Town carries vivid red, hybrid-tea-shaped blooms in generous clusters over dark, glossy foliage, giving a mounded, spreading, own-root shrub the refined flower form of classic roses without the maintenance. Its spreading habit widens as the plant matures, making it as useful in containers as it is massed along a border. Flowering continues steadily from late spring through fall on strong, disease-resistant growth. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil and prune lightly in late winter to keep the spreading shape in bounds.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Pinktopia Rose (Medium Pink Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Pinktopia is an upright Easy Elegance selection whose red new growth contrasts with masses of fragrant medium-pink, semi-double flowers.

directions: Pinktopia smothers itself in semi-double, fragrant medium-pink flowers from late spring until the first fall frost, set against dark green foliage that emerges a contrasting red. The upright, own-root shrub reaches a taller, narrower profile than many Easy Elegance roses, making it useful as an accent plant or informal hedge. Its fragrant blooms also work well as cut flowers. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil; the plant tolerates heat well and needs minimal disease management.
sources: Bailey Nurseries — Easy Elegance Rose Collection

common_name: Super Hero Rose (Red Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Super Hero forms a compact, rounded shrub covered in clusters of red blooms and performs well in both cool and warm climates.

directions: Super Hero produces clusters of perfectly formed red blooms over clean, satiny, medium-to-dark green foliage on a compact, rounded, own-root shrub that can grow larger than many of its Easy Elegance siblings. It handles a wide range of climates well, holding up to both cold winters and hot summers without heavy disease pressure. Its size and rounded form suit it to foundation plantings and mixed borders alike. Plant in full sun with well-drained soil and prune in late winter to control its eventual size.

common_name: Sweet Fragrance Rose (Coral and Apricot Easy Elegance Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant this own-root shrub rose in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sweet Fragrance has an upright habit with hybrid-tea-shaped buds that swirl open into fragrant apricot blossoms.

directions: Sweet Fragrance opens buds tinted coral and orange over a deep yellow base, swirling into full, sweetly scented apricot blossoms shaped like a classic hybrid tea rose. Strong stems and an upright, own-root habit make it a good candidate for cutting gardens as well as borders, and its fragrance sets it apart from many disease-resistant landscape roses bred mainly for bloom volume. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil, and deadhead regularly to keep fresh buds forming through the season. Prune back by about a third in late winter to encourage vigorous new growth.
